_comment: Species definitions. Base stats and presentation only; a live creature's current HP and energy belong to a pal_instance, never here (TECHNICAL_START.md, Pal Data vs Pal Instance). M11 replaces `model` and the colours with real rigged creatures without touching combat code.
_comment_moves: Each species carries a `moves` field (D30, pal progression): {"quick": id, "charged": id}, both ids into data/moves/moves.json. Chosen for flavour fit, not balance -- every move ships at power 1.0 so this is balance-neutral. Related species (an evolution line, a shared archetype) may reuse the same move id on purpose; see data/moves/moves.json for the full pool.
_placeholder: M2 ships coloured capsules on purpose. CLAUDE.md forbids judging creature appeal on placeholders, so these are shaped for READABILITY at combat distance — clearly different silhouettes and clearly different colours — and nothing else.
_comment_catch: `catch_rate` is the species' base share of the catch formula in scripts/combat/catch_math.gd. Lower is rarer. Every species must declare one; tests/test_catch_math.gd fails the build if any is missing, because a creature that is accidentally trivial to catch is the kind of bug nobody reports.
_comment_names: Ids and display names for the wild roster are canon from `docs/art/wild/` — the owner's Meadows Wild Canon Pack, which supersedes `docs/art/ROSTER_MANIFEST.md` for these creatures (`docs/decisions/D13`). The meshes under them do not all match yet: Tuskroot is still a songbird from the Plumberry pack (`docs/decisions/D10`) and is the last stand-in in the table. Bramblebun WAS a duck and is not any more — it was produced properly from its own sheet.
_comment_scale: Creatures stand as PEERS to the 1.8m trainer, not as pets at his ankles (docs/decisions/D12), and the band was raised a second time by the owner's D19 decision: starters at boar scale. Starters 1.90-2.00m, wild pals 1.35-2.15m so GAME_DESIGN.md 26's 'pal size should vary substantially' still holds around the new centre. Radii scale by the SAME ratio as height per D12, so nothing gets easier to hit relative to its own size. The reference sheets' real-world sizes (Terrapup 0.45m at the shoulder) are the CREATURE'S biology, not its game scale, and the two are allowed to differ -- see D12/D19.
_comment_wild_stats: TUNABLE, all of them. The wild roster's statlines are set from the sheets' own ROLE and STRENGTHS lines and from nothing else: a digger is tougher than a scout, a tracker hits harder than it takes, a shell is defence and a raptor is not. Nobody has played a fight with any of them yet, so treat every number below as a first guess that combat feedback is expected to move.
_comment_wild_heights: Heights follow D13's rule (the sheets' RELATIVE ordering is preserved) inside D19's raised band: the owner's decision this pass, starters at boar scale, so the wild roster runs 1.35-2.15m around them. The pack's own centimetre figures (Pipwing 0.25m body length, Galecrest 1.80m) are the creature's biology, not its game scale, exactly as sheets 01-04's figures already are. Pipwing and Bramblebun stay the smallest; Meadowhart, Galecrest and Tuskroot stay the largest.
_comment_evolution_size: An evolution is ALWAYS larger than the form it came from — the owner's rule, `docs/decisions/D17`. Every `evolves_into` target must have a strictly greater `placeholder.height` than its source. This constrains RELATIVE size inside a line only; it does not reopen the settled peer band (D12/D13, recentred by D19 at 1.20-2.60m overall). Mudsnout 1.55m -> Tuskroot 2.15m satisfies it, and the pair satisfied D17 by accident until tests/test_evolution_links.gd started failing loudly on it, because heights here are tunable and a tune that inverts a line is otherwise completely silent.
_comment_aggressive: `aggressive` decides whether a wild pal will start a fight on its own. GAME_DESIGN.md 14 forbids simple proximity starting a fight with a PEACEFUL pal, and the same list allows 'Aggressive pal initiates' — so this flag is the line between those two rules, and it lives in data because it is a property of the creature, not of the code.

placeholder._comment_footprint: How long this body may be for its width, as a multiple of its collider diameter. A quadruped is genuinely several times longer than it is wide; a frog is not. Set too low and pal_body._fit() scales the model DOWN to fit the allowance and the creature renders shorter than its own collider claims — silently, until MA4.
placeholder._comment_art: Rigged and animated. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider — and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus — does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.
placeholder._comment_animations: 26 clips ship baked into each .glb, so nothing is retargeted and nothing can be mangled. `pain` and `fall_over` are what hit and faint have wanted since M2; `uppercut` is a real committed swing rather than a lunge with no animation.
placeholder._comment_size: Chibi bipeds beside a 1.8m trainer, so they read as companions rather than as livestock — which is the Palworld register. Sized against each other so the practice creature is smaller than your partner and the one that ambushes you is bigger than both.
placeholder._comment_pack: Plumberry Plains Vol. 2, and it answers the review's first and largest complaint directly. The critic's words were 'none of them is a designed creature... Palworld's entire proposition is that its creatures are drawn characters — bold silhouette, hue-opposed to the environment, exaggerated proportion, expression', and that the previous roster put 'a naturalistic tree frog, a faceted grey low-poly goat, and a Nintendo Mii in the same 300 pixels'. These are ten designed chibi characters from ONE artist, which fixes the design AND the cohesion complaint at once.
placeholder._comment_pick:
Chosen on MEASURED colour, not taste. The first pick was fox, rabbit and wolf — which turned out to be the three LEAST saturated characters in the pack (0.20, 0.19, 0.15), i.e. exactly the defect the critic named on the creature they replaced: 'saturation 0.12... a grey rock standing on olive ground... your own pal is the least readable object in your own fight'. Re-picked against its stated criterion — hue-opposed to a green world, and readable at 40px:
  bear      hue  23 deg, sat 0.77, val 0.61  — orange-brown, the most saturated thing in the pack
  duck      hue  42 deg, sat 0.67, val 0.95  — bright gold
  songbird  hue 194 deg, sat 0.36, val 0.72  — blue, the only cool hue available
Three hues, three values, none of them the chartreuse the ground is made of.

trailpup._comment: Tracker and flanker. The sheet's strengths are Speed, Tracking, Loyalty, so it is the roster's glass canine: it hits harder than anything else at its size and takes hits worse. Explicitly NOT the Ground starter -- no stone plates anywhere on it, which the canon pack names as a hard distinction.

burrowback._comment: Defender/Excavator per the sheet's own ROLE line, STRENGTHS Defense, Digging, Control. Broad low silhouette built for digging and defense, powerful forelimbs with shovel-like claws, rock nodules for natural armor -- so it carries the roster's highest defence alongside Trailpup's attack lead, not the other way round. Medium size class keeps HP moderate rather than tanky-huge. Non-aggressive: a defender protects territory when approached, it does not hunt. All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

tuskroot._comment_evolution: Tuskroot is no longer a base creature you meet in the wild — the owner's Meadows Wild Canon Pack makes it the evolved form of Mudsnout, and the ONLY evolution in the biome (docs/decisions/D13). Recorded here so the link is not lost. `mudsnout` now exists in this table, so both ends of the link are real; there is still no evolution SYSTEM in the project. The pair's heights (Mudsnout 1.55m -> Tuskroot 2.15m after D19's size pass) are held apart by D17 and tests/test_evolution_links.gd: the evolved form must always be the larger one.

paddlenewt._comment: Quick Swimmer/Skirmisher per the sheet's own subtitle and build notes (Water Sheet, docs/art/reference/wild/03_Meadows_Wild_Water_Sheet.png): agile amphibious body, webbed toes for quick bursts, soft fins for balance and display, moist skin, no armor plating. A skirmisher hits fast and often rather than tanking -- so it carries the roster's lowest defence (soft-bodied, small) with attack in the upper-middle band (Ripplet/Trailpup territory) and HP on the low side for its Small-Medium size class. Non-aggressive: the sheet's own design notes call the whole Water roster 'friendly, expressive... calm spirits', and Paddlenewt's listed actions are WATER DASH and PLAYFUL POUNCE, not a hunting behaviour. Common (small pond creature): catch rate near Bramblebun/Mudsnout, not Tuskroot's rare end. All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

Non-aggressive, matching the sheet's own 'friendly... calm spirits' design note for the whole Water roster and its SHELL RETREAT listed behaviour. Catch rate near Burrowback's (a slow, armoured creature, not a common skittish one). All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

Smallest of the six wild quadrupeds finished so far (1.45m), so HP and defence sit at the low end; attack modest but not the lowest, since 'quick and clever' implies some bite. Non-aggressive, matching the sheet's own 'sociable' framing and its Water-roster-wide 'friendly... calm spirits' design note. All tunable; nobody has fought one yet.

placeholder._comment_art: R0.6: tools/art_pipeline finish.py clean -> texture -> rig -> grade -> install, from the R0.4 winner (candidate a). See docs/art/MEADOWS_WILD_PRODUCTION_REPORT.md. TWO known defects on this creature, both flagged rather than fixed: (1) R0.4 recorded a HARD FAIL shared by every candidate -- the canon's broad flat scaled paddle tail is absent, both candidates give a round tapering tail instead. The report's own instruction is to ship it forward with the defect flagged rather than block or re-roll ('iterating on what exists'), and that a real sculpting pass is separate future work -- not attempted here. (2) rig_quadruped.py's automatic weighting left 35 of 14,034 vertices (0.25%) unweighted, the first species in this batch where residual post-retexture mesh noise (6,075 non-manifold edges, 81 microscopic disconnected components -- the same category every species carries after Meshy's retexture re-unwrap, see Tuskroot's DONE.md entry) actually crossed into un-rigged vertices rather than being silently absorbed. Confirmed scattered across the whole body rather than concentrated at the tail, so not obviously the same root cause as (1); will read as tiny pinned-in-bind-pose specks during animation rather than one visible tear. A proper fix likely needs a fresh clean/remesh pass or the eventual tail sculpt, not attempted here. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider -- and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus -- does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.

galecrest._comment: Sky Soarer/Aerial Striker per the Air Sheet (docs/art/reference/wild/04_Meadows_Wild_Air_Sheet.png): medium-large raptor, powerful wings and hooked beak, 'built for speed, lift, and precise control in strong winds' -- a genuine predator, and D13 explicitly requires it not read like the Air starter Galewisp ('not a starter-like cute fox-bird hybrid'). Highest attack of the wild roster so far and the lowest defence, mirroring Galewisp's own thin-armour/high-attack air profile but pushed further since this one is built to strike, not glide. Marked aggressive, unlike the rest of the wild roster bar Tuskroot -- the sheet's own language ('fierce focused eyes', 'Aerial Striker') reads as a real predator rather than a skittish prey animal. First bird species: first exercise of R0.6's rig --kind bird path (rig_bird.py), see the placeholder art comment below.

placeholder._comment_art: R0.6: first bird species. tools/art_pipeline finish.py clean -> texture -> rig --kind bird -> grade -> install, from the R0.4 winner (candidate a). This run also exercised a fix to finish.py's `rig` command: it previously called animate_quadruped.py unconditionally after rigging, which for a bird would have silently re-detected rig_bird.py's output as a glider (their bone names deliberately overlap) and overwritten rig_bird.py's own already-authored, already-proven six clips with generic glider animation -- including animate_quadruped.py's documented faint-spin bug. finish.py now skips that call when --kind is bird, since rig_bird.py authors all six clips itself. rig_report.json: 19 bones, 14004 vertices, 6 unweighted (0.04%, same noise-level pattern as Brooktail's), idle motion at 108% of walk (well clear of the 6%-is-frozen threshold flagged in rig_bird.py's own self-check). model_yaw not visually verified -- this container has no libEGL.so.1, so turntable.py cannot render a frame, a persistent limitation recorded for every species finished this session; 0.0 follows the same default every quadruped so far shipped with. Two glossy black hooked-beak shapes were checked and rejected as eye_guard candidates in grade.py -- see that file's comment. The model is measured and fitted to `height` at load by pal_body._fit(), so the collider -- and therefore the hit cone and the catch accuracy bonus -- does not move when the art is swapped. `colour` is retained only for the fallback capsule.

_comment_wild_roster: The Meadows wild roster is canonised by docs/art/wild/ — twelve species plus one evolution. Species appear in this file as each is produced, because smoke_art.gd requires every entry to name a model that exists. All twelve wild species have real production art now (R0.6 complete); Tuskroot's evolved-form model is the one remaining stand-in, tracked separately. Heights follow D13's relative ordering inside D19's raised band (starters at boar scale).
